narrative: Material PL3__M1427F84 exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=0.41) with a high activity rate of 93.5% non-zero days, indicating a regularly consumed item without significant intermittency. Lead times average 3.13 working days with moderate variability (CV=0.34), and lead-time variance dominates the demand-during-lead-time uncertainty (85.7% of total variance). The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock, creating material stockout exposure; the recommended (r,Q) policy with 6,188 units of safety stock and a reorder point of 15,077 units is designed to achieve a 95% cycle service level. The storage capacity constraint of 41,351 units caps the order quantity at 35,163 units — below the unconstrained EOQ of 60,012 — but still delivers a 65% annual cost reduction over the current MOQ-based baseline.
warnings: Storage capacity is binding: order quantity capped at 35163 (down from EOQ 60012). This increases ordering frequency relative to the unconstrained optimum.
SAP safety stock is 0; current ERP policy provides no buffer against demand or lead-time variability.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The material has moderate CV (0.41) with high non-zero demand fraction (93.5%), making it well-suited to a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. The presence of a hard MOQ and a binding storage cap favours a fixed-order-quantity approach over periodic review, as it allows precise trigger-based replenishment without over-ordering.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity cap reduces order quantity 41.4% below EOQ (35,163 vs 60,012 units), increasing annual order frequency from ~11.6 to ~19.8 orders/year and raising ordering cost from ~$870 to ~$1,483/year. A storage capacity increase of approximately 19,000 units would unlock full EOQ savings.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (8,817) + safety_stock (6,188) = 15,005 units, which is below max_storage_units (41,351). Policy is feasible with no MOQ-capacity conflict.
